melbheat

melbheat helps a council or emergency-planning officer answer one question: have days above a chosen temperature become more frequent at Melbourne Airport since 1970, and does the answer depend on what counts as “hot”?

Documentation site: https://etc5523-2026.github.io/etc5523-assignment-4-tngu0386-oss/ (function reference and a vignette that walks through the analysis and the app).

Quick start 

library(melbheat)
ex <- annual_exceedances(threshold = 35)   # days a year above 35 °C
plot_exceedances(ex, split_year = 2000)    # chart: 8.2 vs 11.8 days a year

Each year is only counted if at least 80% of its days were recorded, so a partly missing year such as 2022 is shown in grey and left out of the averages.

Installation

Install the development version from GitHub:

# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-tngu0386-oss")

or

# install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("ETC5523-2026/etc5523-assignment-4-tngu0386-oss")

Launch the app 

library(melbheat)
run_app()

The app opens in your browser. Choose whether to count hot days or hot nights, set the temperature threshold, pick the months and a comparison year, then read the summary, the chart and the table. The Does the threshold matter? tab checks the answer across many thresholds, and the Guide tab explains each control, each field and how to read the results.

What is in the package

Function What it does
melb_temp Daily maximum and minimum temperature at Melbourne Airport
annual_exceedances() Days per year above a threshold, flagging years with too many missing days
summarise_periods() Average annual count before and after a chosen year
describe_periods() Plain-language summary: what changed and how sure we are
threshold_sensitivity() The same comparison repeated across many thresholds
plot_exceedances(), plot_sensitivity() ggplot2 charts that state the finding in the title
run_app() Launches the Shiny app

Data

melb_temp holds one row per calendar day from 1 January 1970 to 26 July 2022 for the Melbourne Airport weather station (Bureau of Meteorology station 086282): date, year, month, daily maximum (tmax) and minimum (tmin) temperature in degrees Celsius, and the Bureau’s quality flag for each. Days without an observation are kept as NA. Readings that accumulate over more than one day are set to NA.

Source: Australian Bureau of Meteorology, Climate Data Online, http://www.bom.gov.au/climate/data/ (products IDCJAC0010 and IDCJAC0011). Copyright Commonwealth of Australia, Bureau of Meteorology; used here for educational purposes with attribution. The raw files and the script that prepares them (data-raw/melb_temp.R) are in the repository, so the data set can be rebuilt from scratch. The MIT licence covers the package code, not the data.

Limits

This is one weather station, readings are as recorded (not adjusted for instrument or site changes), and the comparison shows that hot days were more frequent later, not why.
